# Bug ledger

*Generated by `python tools/docs/bugs_ledger.py` from `docs/bugs/defects.json` and `docs/bugs/round2/*.json`; do not edit by hand.*

Before changing anything, the original game was audited by reading every script and running it: **113 verified defects** (each with file, line numbers and evidence), plus **2740 layout violations** found by running the new audit tool over the original `ship.json`. This ledger records how every defect was resolved. **112 of 113 are fixed**; 1 was deliberately kept (with the reason).

## The original layout, measured

`tools/layout/audit.py` checks footprints, walls, windows, ceilings, mounting, department policy, walkability, BOM and lights. Run over the original ship (6,679 props) and the new one (2555 props):

| Rule | What it catches | Original layout | New layout |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tabletop-host` | small items standing on chairs, couches, pillars ... | 943 | 0 |
| `table-support` | table items floating or buried | 470 | 0 |
| `wall-floor-clash` | wall equipment embedded in furniture | 340 | 0 |
| `policy-category` | equipment in the wrong department (beds in engineering ...) | 306 | 0 |
| `footprint-overlap` | furniture intersecting furniture | 142 | 0 |
| `mount-mismatch` | wall models mid-room, ceiling models on the floor | 132 | 0 |
| `outside-shell` | props inside walls / outside the room | 87 | 0 |
| `floating-floor` | floor props not on the floor | 77 | 0 |
| `too-tall` | props taller than the room | 55 | 0 |
| `duplicates` | the same model over and over (warning) | 55 | 5 |
| `ceiling-floor-clash` | ceiling items inside tall furniture | 39 | 0 |
| `wall-item-overlap` | wall items overlapping | 27 | 0 |
| `unreachable-pocket` | floor the player cannot reach (warning) | 22 | 3 |
| `wall-item-span` | wall items past the end of the wall | 12 | 0 |
| `ceiling-overlap` | ceiling items overlapping | 11 | 0 |
| `lights` | rooms without light fixtures | 9 | 0 |
| `window-blocked` | tall props in front of windows | 6 | 0 |
| `aisle-width` | passages under 0.8 m (warning) | 5 | 7 |
| `door-clearance` | props in a doorway | 1 | 0 |
| `unknown-room-policy` | rooms the policy does not know (warning) | 1 | 0 |
| **total** | | **2740** | **15** |

(The new layout's remaining entries are warnings only: aisle-width x7, duplicates x5, unreachable-pocket x3.)

## Defects

### B001 - Stale body_exited of the old lift clears player.lift after a teleport

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity / area | high / godot-runtime |
| Where | `godot/scripts/lift.gd` lines 18-19 |
| Status | **fixed** |

*Evidence.* Ran ShipBuilder+player headless: player placed in Lift_A1 -> player.lift=Lift_A1; go_to_deck(2) teleports (y=4.08); after 60 physics frames the player stands in Lift_A2 but player.lift == null. The exited-handler (`if _player == b: _player = null; b.set("lift", null)`) fires for A1 after/around A2's entered-handler and unconditionally nulls the shared pointer.

*Impact.* After the first hop the turbolift prompt disappears and keys 1/2/3 do nothing until the player walks out and back in; chained hops (1->3) are impossible.

*Resolution.* The lifts are gone. Stairs are plain geometry, there is no teleport and no `lift` pointer on the player (`godot/scripts/lift.gd` deleted). `godot/tests/stair_test.gd` walks the player up and down both towers.

### B002 - generate_normals() smooths normals across box corners: every wall/floor/ceiling box is shaded like a pillow

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity / area | high / godot-builder |
| Where | `godot/scripts/ship_builder.gd` lines 100-115 |
| Status | **fixed** |

*Evidence.* Godot 4.7 probe: SurfaceTool.append_from(BoxMesh) then generate_normals() changes all 24 vertex normals (sample (0,0,1) -> (-0.667,0.667,0.333)) because smooth_group defaults to 0. The shell meshes are built exactly this way (st.generate_normals(); st.generate_tangents()), so large flat wall quads interpolate corner-averaged normals (and tangents for the normal maps).

*Impact.* Incorrect lighting gradients across every wall, floor and ceiling; normal maps derive from wrong tangents.

*Resolution.* The shell is built from explicit prisms with flat per-face normals (`ShipBuilder.Shell.prism`), no `generate_normals()` smoothing.

### B003 - `margin` in Room.free() shrinks existing footprints instead of growing them, so clearance permits overlap

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity / area | high / layout-engine |
| Where | `tools/layout/shiplib.py` lines 184-192 |
| Status | **fixed** |

*Evidence.* Condition `x0 < a[2] - margin and x1 > a[0] + margin ...`. Demo: foot=(4,4,5,5); rect (4.8,4,6,5) overlapping by 0.2 m -> free(margin=0.25) == True but free(margin=0) == False. Callers rely on margin as clearance: place_anywhere (margin=0.25), cargo_bay (0.25), store_leftovers (0.15), pack_depot (0.05).

*Impact.* Clearance passes make overlaps more likely (82 overlapping floor-prop pairs in the committed ship.json) and break the README walkway promise.

*Resolution.* `Room.free()` now calls `polys_overlap(corners, other, margin)` with the margin as required clearance. `tests/test_shiplib.py::test_margin_grows_the_clearance_instead_of_shrinking_it`.

### B004 - run(wall_mount=True) forces wall_item() for every model, mounting floor/ceiling/table models on the wall

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity / area | high / layout-engine |
| Where | `tools/layout/shiplib.py` lines 349-350 |
| Status | **fixed** |

*Evidence.* Committed ship.json: 76 floor-mount props hover above the deck (>5 cm) (e.g. comms commsunit_comms_console y=9.6, commsunit_radio_rack y=9.6, router_wireless_tower; 15 junction, 12 router, 11 sign, 9 sciinstrument, 8 commsunit...), 28 ceiling-mount models sit at wall height 1.5 m (galley pipe_ceiling_pump/pipe_ceiling_turn/pipe_ceiling_tee at y=5.5), 42 table-mount items hang on walls (comms commsunit_radio_transceiver y=9.6). 63 of the floating floor props also get solid colliders at that height (ship_builder.gd:300-309).

*Impact.* Floating equipment, invisible colliders at head height, wrong-looking rooms (comms centre, galleys, corridors).

*Resolution.* `Room.run(wall_mount=True)` only considers wall-mount models (and floor rows only floor/wall models). `test_run_with_wall_mount_hangs_only_wall_models`.

### B005 - light_grid/dress_ceiling place non-ceiling models at ceiling height: 100 wall-mount models stuck sideways in ceilings

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity / area | high / layout-engine |
| Where | `tools/layout/shiplib.py` lines 373-389 |
| Status | **fixed** |

*Evidence.* light_room(cats=('ceilinglight','panellight')) (recipes: corridors, lobbies, galley, medbay, sci, life, core, cargoB) and dress_ceiling(cats=('ceilingpanel','duct')) / airlock cats ('ceilinglight','beacon') pick any model and call place(..., y=R.y+R.h). ship.json: 100 wall-mount props sit at y==ceiling (84 panellight, 10 duct, 6 beacon; medbay 16, cor2 12, cargoB 12, cor1 8, galley 8, sci 8...), oriented as wall plates sticking out of the ceiling; + 29 table-mount items also at ceiling y (see pillar item).

*Impact.* Ceilings carry sideways panels half inside the slab (e.g. cor1 panellight_window_light_box pokes 0.45 m above the ceiling).

*Resolution.* `light_grid` only picks ceiling models and `place()` refuses wall models and wrong heights. `test_place_refuses_wall_models_and_wrong_heights`, audit rule `mount-mismatch`.

### B006 - Python 3.11 + unpinned `pip install bpy` contradicts the bpy requirement

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity / area | high / ci |
| Where | `.github/workflows/ci.yml` lines 15-16,42-49 |
| Status | **fixed** |

*Evidence.* PYTHON_VERSION="3.11" with comment 'bpy (headless Blender 5.x module) needs Python 3.11'; per the project brief/PyPI metadata the latest bpy (5.2, the version README says was used) requires Python 3.13, so an unpinned `pip install bpy numpy` on 3.11 either fails to resolve or silently installs an older release (kit.py needs Blender 4.2+ APIs such as surface_render_method). Not reproduced offline; based on the stated requirement.

*Impact.* The blender job (45 min) is red or not testing the Blender the project targets.

*Resolution.* CI runs Python 3.13 and installs `requirements-blender.txt` (`bpy>=5.2,<6`), the latest headless Blender.

### B007 - `or true` makes the mouse-captured check dead; player walks while mouse is released / map is open

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity / area | medium / godot-runtime |
| Where | `godot/scripts/player.gd` lines 82-87 |
| Status | **fixed** |

*Evidence.* `if Input.mouse_mode == Input.MOUSE_MODE_CAPTURED or true:` always true, so WASD keeps moving the body after Esc (mouse visible) and while the M deck-map overlay covers the screen.

*Impact.* Player drifts/walks blind while using the map or after Esc; the guard is clearly intended but inert.

*Resolution.* `player.gd` no longer has the dead `or true`; movement uses the simulated/real input vector only, the mouse is released on `ui_cancel`, focus loss and while the map is open.

### B008 - Door trigger volume (3.6x2.6x3.8 m) reaches the corridor centre line so doors open for passers-by

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity / area | medium / godot-runtime |
| Where | `godot/scripts/door.gd` lines 37-47 |
| Status | **fixed** |

*Evidence.* abox.size=(3.6,2.6,3.8), local Z = door normal; corridors (cor1/cor2/cor3) are 4 m wide with doors on both side walls at x=+-2, so the trigger spans x in [-3.9,-0.1] / [0.1,3.9]: walking down either half of the corridor opens every door you pass (25 doors, each plays the door sound).

*Impact.* Doors constantly slide/clunk while just walking along corridors; closed-door feel and audio are lost.

*Resolution.* `door.gd` trigger is the door width + 0.6 m wide and 2.2 m deep (1.1 m each side of the door plane) instead of 3.6 x 3.8 m.

### B009 - Tour mode hangs forever without a renderer: null image is not checked and quit() is never reached

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity / area | medium / godot-runtime |
| Where | `godot/scripts/main.gd` lines 188-195 |
| Status | **fixed** |

*Evidence.* Ran `godot --headless --path godot -- --tour=/tmp/x --only=01_bridge`: `ERROR: Parameter "t" is null` at main.gd:190 then `SCRIPT ERROR: Cannot call method 'save_png' on a null value` (main.gd:192); the coroutine aborts before get_tree().quit(), process still running after 40 s (killed by timeout, exit 124).

*Impact.* CI screenshot step (continue-on-error) can burn the whole 60-minute job timeout when the GPU/Vulkan backend is unavailable; local --tour runs hang.

*Resolution.* `main.gd` tour checks the rendered image and exits with status 1 and a message when there is no renderer or the file cannot be written.

### B010 - No occlusion culling at all despite the comment (“meshes + collision + occluders”)

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity / area | medium / perf |
| Where | `godot/scripts/ship_builder.gd` lines 88-93,281-318 |
| Status | **fixed** |

*Evidence.* Headless probe of the built ship: OccluderInstance3D count = 0, 7,029 MeshInstance3D; props are culled only by distance (visibility_range_end 16/28/48/90 m by size, 60 m for doors) so the contents of every room/deck within range is submitted each frame.

*Impact.* Draw cost scales with the whole ship rather than the visible room.

*Resolution.* Every room builds an `OccluderInstance3D` from its wall/slab prisms and `occlusion_culling/use_occlusion_culling=true` is set in `project.godot`.

### B011 - Every prop is its own scene instance: 6,679 instances, 16,591 nodes, ~40,984 surfaces, 3.75 M triangles

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity / area | medium / perf |
| Where | `godot/scripts/ship_builder.gd` lines 281-310 |
| Status | **fixed** |

*Evidence.* Measured: ship built in 1.18 s, nodes=16591, meshes=7029; summing glTF primitives over placements gives 40,984 surfaces (median 6 per prop) and 3,751,242 triangles (README quotes 707k for the library only). 2,151 of the props are tiny table-mounted items (tableware, lamps, terminals).

*Impact.* High draw-call/node count, long load and scene-tree overhead; small clutter dominates cost.

*Resolution.* Props are batched into MultiMeshes per (room, model mesh) instead of one scene instance each, and the ship has 1.4 k props instead of 6.7 k. Measured: 17,950 -> ~355 draw calls, 16.6 k -> 3.5 k nodes (see README).

### B012 - 474 of 907 shell collision shapes are sub-5 cm trim boxes

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity / area | medium / perf |
| Where | `godot/scripts/ship_builder.gd` lines 94-114 |
| Status | **fixed** |

*Evidence.* Probe: Shell StaticBody3D holds 907 CollisionShape3D; 474 have a dimension <0.05 m (baseboard `hull` 0.14x0.02, `trim` stripe 0.06x0.02, window frames/mullions) because every non-glow box gets a collider. Plus 1,318 prop shapes.

*Impact.* Needless broadphase/physics cost and snag potential along walls for zero gameplay value (the wall itself already stops the capsule).

*Resolution.* Trim boxes (baseboard, stripe, cove) are visual only; they no longer get collision shapes (`prism(..., collide=false)`).

### B013 - 98 of 279 lights cast shadows (35%)

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity / area | medium / perf |
| Where | `godot/scripts/ship_builder.gd` lines 256-262 |
| Status | **fixed** |

*Evidence.* ship.json: 279 lights, 98 with shadow=true (light_grid shadow_every=3/2/4) plus the player flashlight shadow; soft_shadow_filter_quality=3 (Soft Medium) for positional and directional shadows in project.godot and shadow_blur=1.5 on every light; no shadow atlas/size settings.

*Impact.* Dozens of shadow-map renders when several rooms are in range; large frame-time cost on mid GPUs.

*Resolution.* At most 2 (3 in rooms over 150 m2) shadow-casting lights per room are kept; props under 0.6 m do not cast shadows.

### B014 - Heavy post/AA stack is always on with no quality setting

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity / area | medium / perf |
| Where | `godot/project.godot` lines 91-97 |
| Status | **fixed** |

*Evidence.* msaa_3d=2 (4x), anisotropic level 3, soft shadow quality 3; main.gd:127-142 enables SSAO (radius 1.4), volumetric fog (length 36), glow and adjustments unconditionally; the only escape hatches are --no-fog/--no-probes cmdline flags used by CI, nothing in-game.

*Impact.* MSAA 4x + SSAO + volumetric fog + 34 reflection probes + 98 shadow lights on 3.7 M triangles is unusable on integrated GPUs.

*Resolution.* Balanced default (FXAA, cheap depth haze, half-resolution SSAO); volumetric fog, 4x MSAA are behind `--hq`.

### B015 - place() does not honour a model's mount; wall-mount models dropped mid-room via R.place(pick('table'/'bench'))

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity / area | medium / layout-engine |
| Where | `tools/layout/shiplib.py` lines 194-222 |
| Status | **fixed** |

*Evidence.* 5 wall-mount props stand far from any wall at y=mount_y: capt table_fold_down_table (7.8,8.9,22.68) is 5.3 m from the nearest wall, dorm table_fold_down_table 4.7 m, mess bench_padded_wall_bench (-12.99,4.9,-4.4) 5.0 m, hydro bench_padded_wall_bench 2.8 m, comms desk_fold_down_wall_desk. Recipes call c.pick('table'/'bench') without a mount predicate and place() accepts wall models.

*Impact.* Floating furniture in mid-air; table items are then stacked on the floating table.

*Resolution.* `Room.place()` honours the model mount: wall models are refused, floor models stay on the floor, ceiling models at the ceiling.

### B016 - Catalog.pen (placement-failure penalty) leaks across rooms and is never reset

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity / area | medium / layout-engine |
| Where | `tools/layout/shiplib.py` lines 32,45,58 |
| Status | **fixed** |

*Evidence.* dressing.py:226 adds 0.5 to cat.pen[id] per failed garnish placement and pick()/pick_any() add pen to the use count forever. After build() 125 models carry penalties (bed_fold_down_wall_bed 20.5, shelving_parts_bin_wall 18.5, antenna_phased_array_panel 17.5, hangartool_wall_winch 17.5).

*Impact.* A failure in one room permanently de-prioritises that model in every later room (output depends on room order) and pushes those models to the leftover dump.

*Resolution.* `Catalog.pen` was removed; there is no placement-failure state left to leak across rooms.

### B017 - Tabletop hosts include every floor prop with top_y>=0.45: 243 small items stand on chairs, couches, benches, bins, bots, pillars...

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity / area | medium / layout-engine |
| Where | `tools/layout/dressing.py` lines 170,232 |
| Status | **fixed** |

*Evidence.* Hosts are chosen only by top_y (place_anywhere line 170, tabletop_pass line 232). Counted table items resting on hosts of category: couch 61, bench 44, chair 40, pillar 29, forcefield 20, bin 16, cylinder 16, cleaningbot 8, seat 6, lamp 2, fountain 1 (=243). Examples: lamp_table_lamp + terminal_datapad on chair_gaming_chair (ready room), terminal_laptop_console + lamp on seat_captain_command_chair, galley_microwave on bin_recycling_bin_triple (lounge), instrument_astrolabe on forcefield_shield_doorway (armory).

*Impact.* Nonsensical props (microwave on a bin, lamp on the captain's chair).

*Resolution.* `Room.on_top` only accepts hosts from `shiplib.SURFACE_HOSTS` (tables, desks, benches, counters, racks ...). Audit rule `tabletop-host` (old layout: 943 violations, new: 0).

### B018 - Full-height pillars are table hosts: 33 items placed at ceiling height

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity / area | medium / layout-engine |
| Where | `tools/layout/dressing.py` lines 170,232 |
| Status | **fixed** |

*Evidence.* Corridor pillars (pillar_square_plinth/fluted_round/truss, top_y=3.4) pass the top_y>=0.45 host test; 33 table-mount items (plant_bonsai, plant_flower_vase, lamp_architect_desk_lamp...) sit at y==ceiling in cor1/cor2/cor3 (e.g. cor1 plant_bonsai [-1.66,11.4,1.29] on pillar_square_plinth), i.e. inside the ceiling slab.

### B019 - on_top() stacks items at random offsets with no collision check: 859 overlapping table-item pairs, 120 overhanging their host

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity / area | medium / layout-engine |
| Where | `tools/layout/shiplib.py` lines 298-315 |
| Status | **fixed** |

*Evidence.* tabletop()/tabletop_pass pick dx,dz = uniform(+-0.3*w/d) per item with place(check=False). Counted 859 pairs of table items at the same height with overlapping footprints (e.g. bridge lamp_decorative_lantern vs tableware_condiments at (4.37,9.42,-24.46)) and 120 items whose footprint extends >0.10 m beyond the host top. on_top also ignores host scale/pitch.

*Impact.* Interpenetrating clutter and items hanging off desk edges.

*Resolution.* `on_top` keeps the footprints of the items already on a host and rejects overlaps and overhangs. `test_table_items_only_on_work_surfaces_and_never_overlap`; audit `table-support`.

### B020 - against_wall/place ignore wall_used for windows except for tall items: floor props block windows

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity / area | medium / layout-engine |
| Where | `tools/layout/shiplib.py` lines 234-257 |
| Status | **fixed** |

*Evidence.* Only against_wall checks wall_used and only for items taller than 0.6 m; R.place, place_anywhere, grid and recipes bypass it. 12 floor/table props stand within 2 m in front of a window span above the sill: lounge 7 (cabinet_utility_cabinet at (-11.89,-2.43), h=1.83, 1.83 m from the W window), bridge 3 (holo_star_map_globe, plant_ficus_tree, instrument_sextant), captain's quarters 2.

*Impact.* Contradicts README 'windows are never blocked'.

*Resolution.* Windows reserve their wall span and the audit rule `window-blocked` (floor props taller than 0.6 m within 0.5 m of a window) runs in CI; the new ship has 0.

### B021 - Floor items placed after wall items never check wall-mounted props: 220 wall items are embedded in tall floor props

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity / area | medium / layout-engine |
| Where | `tools/layout/shiplib.py` lines 244-247,265-288 |
| Status | **fixed** |

*Evidence.* against_wall only blocks on entries with uy1>=50 (doors/windows); wall-mount props register (y0,y1) in wall_used but floor placement via place()/place_anywhere/garnish ignores them. 220 wall-mount props intersect floor-prop volumes (>5 cm in all axes): lounge 20, conf 18, astro 18, cabin2 17, mess 14, rec 12, capt 11, cargoA 10, comms 8, medbay 8 ...; e.g. bridge display_ticker_banner (-9.85,10.7,-28.16) inside antenna_lattice_mast.

*Impact.* Screens/panels hidden behind or inside cabinets and masts.

*Resolution.* `place()` and `wall_item()` check each other: a wall item cannot intersect a tall floor prop and vice versa (`vboxes`). Audit `wall-floor-clash` (old layout 340, new 0).

### B022 - Ceiling placements skip overlap checks (check=False) and any height check against floor props

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity / area | medium / layout-engine |
| Where | `tools/layout/shiplib.py` lines 211-217,373-389 |
| Status | **fixed** |

*Evidence.* light_grid, ceiling_item, corridor camera/beacon and several recipes call place(..., check=False); ship.json: 10 ceiling-ceiling overlaps (cor1 4: duct_ceiling_square_diffuser vs camera_cluster_ceiling, cor3 3, cor2 2, brig 1) and 32 ceiling props whose volume intersects a tall floor prop (eng 8, secoff 6, galley 4, cor3 4, comms 2: e.g. comms ceilingpanel_light_recess_2x2 through router_wireless_tower/antenna_lattice_mast).

### B023 - garnish() adds unlimited non-floor items after the occupancy target is met and is department-wide rather than room-aware

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity / area | medium / layout-engine |
| Where | `tools/layout/dressing.py` lines 205-227 |
| Status | **fixed** |

*Evidence.* `(low or c['mount'] != 'floor')` keeps adding wall/ceiling/table items up to max_new (70/35) per room regardless of target; corridors (transit target 0.05) end with cor1 274, cor2 289, cor3 291 props (854 = 12.7% of all props for 3 x 4 m strips). GARNISH lists are per department, so equipment lands in wrong rooms (see data items).

*Impact.* Cluttered walkways, wrong equipment, inflated node count.

*Resolution.* The random garnish pass is deleted. Every item comes from a written BOM line (`R.line`) and the placement policy (`tools/layout/policy.py`).

### B024 - Bridge recipe: forward stations and rear seats are silently dropped

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity / area | medium / layout-engine |
| Where | `tools/layout/recipes_deck1.py` lines 17-40 |
| Status | **fixed** |

*Evidence.* against_wall('N', console, x, gap=0.55) (line 22) returns None because the N wall is one 15 m window (wall_used y0..99); 0 consoles exist within 3 m of the window wall in ship.json. seat_behind(con=None) returns None. Rear stations (line 36-38) use gap=-1.3: only 2 consoles at the S wall and the bridge has just 3 seats (captain + 2).

*Impact.* 'Bridge stations facing the viewport' (README) do not exist; main set piece is empty near the window.

*Resolution.* The recipe helpers record every placement that does not fit (`RECIPE_DEBUG=1` prints them) and the audit fails on BOM lines without props (`bom-line`); the bridge now has its helm, ops, tactical and seats, all audited.

### B027 - Computer Core: 59% of the free floor area is unreachable on foot

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity / area | medium / layout-data |
| Where | `godot/data/ship.json` lines rooms['core'].props |
| Status | **fixed** |

*Impact.* Two thirds of the core are decoration you cannot walk into; screenshot 20 looks fine but play does not.

*Resolution.* Computer Core is re-laid in hot/cold-aisle pods; the `walkable` audit proves every cell of the room is reachable.

### B029 - _line() negative slice indices wrap around: hazard screen texture is wrong

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity / area | medium / blender |
| Where | `blender/starship/textures.py` lines 80-85,493-498 |
| Status | **fixed** |

*Evidence.* `img[max(0,y-w//2):y+w//2+1, max(0,x-w//2):x+w//2+1]` - for x<0 the stop index is negative and selects from the far side. scr_hazard draws lines from x=-256..: 9,478 of 65,536 pixels differ from a correctly clipped render, and a line fully off-screen (x=-100..-80) paints 534 pixels. screen:hazard is used (bridge.py:1088).

*Impact.* Corrupted hazard stripes texture (and any future off-canvas line).

*Resolution.* `textures._line()` clips both slice bounds (9,478 wrong hazard-screen pixels fixed).

*Resolution.* `tests/test_project.py` checks polygon containment, hull convexity, taper, stair geometry and BOM completeness; `tests/test_audit.py` unit-tests all 30 audit rules and runs them over the committed ship.

|---|---|

*Impact.* Future rooms may receive identical furniture scatter.

*Resolution.* Room RNG seeds use `zlib.crc32(room id)`. `test_room_rng_seed_is_unique_per_id`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity / area | low / blender |
| Where | `blender/starship/textures.py` lines 237-243 |
| Status | **fixed** |

*Evidence.* ys = clip(normal(.5,.22)*h, 0, h-1): 261 of 12,160 stars (2%) land on rows 0 and 1023, forming a bright line at the poles; uniform-per-pixel placement on an equirect image also clusters stars at the poles.

*Impact.* Visible streaks/clumping at the zenith/nadir of the panorama.

*Resolution.* Star latitudes sampled with `arcsin(uniform)` (no pole line).

| Where | `.gitignore` lines 24-26 |

*Evidence.* `.gitignore` ignores *.import (comment says they are regenerated) while .uid files for scripts are committed; Godot 4 expects the .import sidecars to be under version control so UIDs/import options are stable across machines.

*Impact.* UIDs of imported GLBs/textures can differ per clone; per-asset import settings (e.g. normal-map flags for *_normal.png) cannot be committed.

*Resolution.* Kept on purpose: the ~2,600 machine-generated `.import` sidecars stay ignored and are regenerated by `godot --import` (README, CI); committing them would bury this change. Script `.uid` files are committed as before.

### B112 - Preview script always needs xvfb-run and its exit status is lost

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity / area | low / config |
| Where | `tools/preview/run.sh` lines 10 |
| Status | **fixed** |

*Evidence.* `xvfb-run ... | grep -v -E 'ALSA|audio|dummy|^$'`: pipeline status is grep's (exit 1 when all output is filtered, 0 when Godot fails), it also removes any error line containing 'audio'; $GODOT is unquoted; comment says xvfb only 'when no display'.

*Impact.* Failures are masked / success can report exit 1.

*Resolution.* `tools/preview/run.sh` validates its arguments, uses xvfb only without a display and preserves the exit status.

### B113 - preview.gd crashes with no arguments and divides by zero for zero models

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity / area | low / config |
| Where | `tools/preview/preview.gd` lines 8-12 |
| Status | **fixed** |

*Evidence.* `var out_path: String = args[0]` without a size check; n=0 gives cols=0 and `float(n)/cols`.

*Impact.* Unhelpful engine error.

*Resolution.* `preview.gd` prints usage instead of crashing with no arguments.

### B114 [P001] - Room.wall_item() bookkeeps wall items as +-size/2 around their origin; 64 of 274 wall models are not centred, so overlaps and over-ceiling items are accepted

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity / area | high / layout-engine |
| Where | `tools/layout/shiplib.py` lines 549-552, 565-566 |
| Status | **fixed** |

*Evidence.* Fuzz (random against_wall / wall_item / run calls on the unfurnished ship, audited with the committed rules; 10 seeds): 21 wall-item-overlap and 3 wall-item-span errors. Minimal case: table_fold_down_table (bounds y -0.04..0.40, mount_y 0.9 -> real extent 0.86..1.30 m) and antenna_feed_horn_panel (y 1.5 -> 1.15..1.85 m) on the same N-wall span were both accepted (engine recorded 0.68..1.12 for the table); pipe_elbow_up (bounds y -0.073..0.97, size 1.043) at y=2.5 in a 3.4 m room reaches 3.47 m but passed the `yy + size/2 > h - 0.02` check.

*Impact.* Wall items could overlap or poke through the ceiling whenever the engine said they fitted; only the recipes' luck kept the committed ship clean. The generator output now differs (1405 placements instead of 1401: a digital message board that was wrongly refused is placed).

*Resolution.* Fixed in Room.wall_item. Tests: test_P001_wall_item_bookkeeping_uses_the_real_vertical_extent, test_P001_wall_item_top_is_checked_against_the_ceiling_with_real_bounds, test_P002_engine_and_audit_agree_on_random_wall_placements (fuzz). Committed ship still has 0 audit errors.

### B115 [P002] - The engine lets tall floor props stand next to windows; only the audit rule window-blocked (0.5 m) knew about the clearance

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity / area | high / layout-engine |
| Where | `tools/layout/shiplib.py` lines 434-470 (place), 400-420 (add_window) |
| Status | **fixed** |

*Evidence.* Fuzz, 10 seeds, windows from hull_windows(): 195 window-blocked errors from Room.against_wall / place (e.g. specimen_containment_cylinder 2.23 m tall, 0.39 m from a window; plant_ficus_tree 1.94 m, 0.34 m). against_wall only compares the wall span +-0.1 m, place() never looks at windows.

*Impact.* Any recipe that places a tall prop near a window silently produces an audit failure (or, before the audit existed, a blocked view); the engine and the audit disagreed on what is allowed.

*Resolution.* Fixed in Room.add_window / Room.place. Tests: test_P002_engine_keeps_tall_floor_props_clear_of_windows and the fuzz test above. Committed ship output unchanged by this fix.

### B116 [P003] - wall-floor-clash and ceiling-floor-clash have no tolerance: flush items rounded to 1 mm are reported as clashes

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity / area | medium / audit |
| Where | `tools/layout/audit.py` lines 611-621, 632-640 |
| Status | **fixed** |

*Evidence.* Fuzz: `wall item tank_expansion_tank (lowest point 1.14 m) collides with floor prop loader_hand_pallet_jack (1.14 m tall)` and a clock vs a scrubber with a 0.001 m2 'overlap' although the engine (1 mm tolerance in _vclash / wall_item) accepted them. positions in ship.json are rounded to 1 mm, footprint-overlap already needs 5 mm depth, these two rules compared with `<=` / `> 1e-6` and an area-only threshold.

*Impact.* False errors (and false confidence: the same rule cannot be both strict and tolerant for the same geometry), so engine-valid layouts fail the audit depending on rounding.

*Resolution.* Fixed in audit.check_room. Test: test_P003_touching_and_millimetre_contacts_are_not_clashes (also proves a real clash still fires).

### B163 [G001] - Shell.prism(): every side face of every shell prism is inside-out (outward-normal test inverted)

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity / area | critical / render/shell |
| Where | `godot/scripts/ship_builder.gd` lines 88-96 |
| Status | **fixed** |

*Evidence.* `if area > 0.0: nrm = -nrm` flips (d.y, 0, -d.x), which already is the outward normal of a counter-clockwise polygon. Unit probe: a unit prism built from CCW points and from CW points both gave 8 of 8 side triangles whose stored normal points INTO the prism. In the built ship the room-facing face of the north wall of `core` (z = -12.85) stored n = (0,0,-1). Shell.tri() derives the winding from the normal, so the room-facing faces were back-face culled and all walls, baseboards, window frames, glass and cladding were drawn by their FAR faces: walls 15 cm behind their colliders, frames/reveals inside-out (compare tour 01_bridge before/after: the white 'ghost pillars' around the windows are gone), every coplanar analysis ran on the wrong faces.

*Impact.* Walls, trims, frames and plating rendered 3-15 cm away from where they collide, window reveals inside-out, lighting normals of the visible faces reversed relative to the geometry; hid the real z-fights listed below (G023..G035).

*Resolution.* Re-verified on the 5-deck tree: a unit prism from CCW points had 8 of 8 side triangles with the normal pointing into the prism. Fixed in ship_builder.gd Shell.prism. | hunter: ship_builder.gd Shell.prism fixed. Kept fixed by godot/tests/round2_test.gd::_test_prism_normals (both windings + the core wall face) and by zfight_test, which now analyses the correct faces.

### B164 [G002] - All 56 PBR surface / screen / sky PNGs are imported WITHOUT mipmaps: floors, walls, ceiling tiles and the sky shimmer and crawl while walking

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity / area | critical / render/textures |
| Where | `godot/project.godot` lines [importer_defaults] (new) / textures/surfaces, textures/screens, textures/sky |
| Status | **fixed** |

*Evidence.* `godot --import` writes `mipmaps/generate=false` (the editor's 'detect 3D' never runs headless): 56 of 56 textures/*.png.import files (33 of them the surface maps used by ShipMaterials.surface) had it off. Probe: `load('res://textures/surfaces/hull_panel_albedo.png').get_image().has_mipmaps()` == false for hull_panel_albedo, deck_plate_normal, ceiling_orm, screens/alert, sky/stars, sky/planet. The materials ask for LINEAR_WITH_MIPMAPS_ANISOTROPIC, but there is no mip chain to filter with, so a 512 px texture tiled every 4 m is point-minified (about 6 texels per pixel at 20 m) and sparkles with every camera movement. Measured with the new godot/tests/flicker_check.gd (7 cameras, shader time frozen, mean |dL| between frames 1 mm apart; ALL round-2 fixes together, mipmaps being the dominant texture term): original -> fixed ship 01_bridge 0.00176 -> 0.00129, 02_corF1 0.00153 -> 0.00118, 12_hydro 0.00232 -> 0.00220, 14_armory 0.00339 -> 0.00324, 19_life 0.00242 -> 0.00210, 22_hangar 0.00137 -> 0.00114, 23_towerA2 0.00350 -> 0.00268 (-4 .. -27 %); pixels flickering > 6 % luma: tower 1.065 % -> 0.825 %, armory 0.889 % -> 0.844 %.

*Impact.* The 'lot of textures that are flickering' the user reports: every textured surface of the ship at a distance.

*Resolution.* Re-verified: project.godot already had texture mipmaps/generate=true (importer default), but that only affects NEW imports. Ported scripts/texture_fix.gd (TextureFix.fix_tree, called at the end of ShipBuilder.build) as the load-time repair for stale .import files. | hunter: project.godot + godot/scripts/texture_fix.gd + ShipBuilder.build() calls TextureFix.fix_tree(self). Kept fixed by godot/tests/round2_test.gd::_test_textures (every surface kind has mips, forced TextureFix conversion yields a mipmapped ImageTexture, the import file itself says mipmaps on). Existing checkouts: delete the untracked *.png.import files and re-run godot --import (the runtime repair covers them meanwhile).

### B179 [G017] - Head bob teleports the camera up to 28 mm at every start of walking

| Where | `godot/scripts/player.gd` lines 96-109 |
| Status | **fixed** |

### B184 [G022] - Ambient hum / engine rumble loops are cut at 3.2 s of an 8 s clip (QOA-compressed WAVs)

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity / area | high / audio |
| Where | `godot/scripts/main.gd` lines 83-94 |
| Status | **fixed** |

*Evidence.* The importer's default `compress/mode=2` (QOA) makes AudioStreamWAV.format == 3. `_loop()` only knows 16/8-bit and set loop_end = data.size() / 1 = 71408 'frames' (3.24 s at 22050 Hz) for a clip of 176400 frames (8.0 s). Probe: ambient_hum.wav fmt=3 bytes=71408 len=8.0.

*Impact.* The loop restarts in the middle of the waveform every 3.2 s (audible click / pulsing hum).

*Resolution.* Re-verified: the loop length is now loop_frames() (length x mix_rate); project.godot [importer_defaults] wav compress/mode=0. NOTE: .import files are git-ignored, so a stale local cache keeps QOA until godot/audio/*.wav.import is deleted and `godot --import` is re-run; round2_test::_test_audio_loops reports this. | hunter: main.gd + project.godot. Kept fixed by godot/tests/round2_test.gd::_test_audio_loops.

### B201 [A001] - Catalog GLBs are not byte-reproducible: bevel output order follows pointer addresses

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity / area | high / blender/kit |
| Where | `blender/starship/kit.py` lines 222-236 (Model._tag), 440-520 (canonical_order), 640-660 (export) |
| Status | **fixed** |

*Evidence.* Building --only '^(console|desk)_' twice into two directories gave 26 of 30 differing GLBs (same vertex positions, different index buffers). _tag collected bmesh faces/edges in Python sets (address order) and bmesh.ops.bevel orders its result by pointer, so the exported vertex/index order changed per run (door_medical, console_weapons, desk_* ...). arch.canonicalize existed only for the arch assets.

*Impact.* Every rebuild rewrites hundreds of binaries (noisy diffs, impossible to review), CI cannot ever compare GLBs, and the 'reproducible assets' claim in ARCH.md is false for the catalog.

*Resolution.* All 1198 GLBs rebuilt twice with --jobs 4 and --jobs 3 are byte-identical (cmp over every file). tests/test_regress_assets.py::Deterministic builds a model subset twice (needs STARSHIP_BPY_PYTHON, skipped otherwise) and the new CI step 'Rebuilding gives byte-identical GLBs' does the same on every push.

### B202 [A002] - sphere(clip_y) and prism() pass Python sets of BMesh elements to bmesh operators

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity / area | medium / blender/kit |
| Where | `blender/starship/kit.py` lines 271-272 (sphere clip_y), 332 (prism recalc_face_normals) |
| Status | **fixed** |

*Evidence.* `edges = {e for v in verts for e in v.link_edges}` / `faces = {f ...}` feed bisect_plane and `list({fc for ...})` feeds recalc_face_normals; set iteration order is memory-address order, so the operators saw their input in a different order on every run (same class of bug as A001).

*Impact.* Dome and prism meshes (ceiling domes, wedges) could come out with a different triangulation/winding order between runs.

*Resolution.* tests/test_regress_assets.py::Deterministic::test_kit_never_iterates_sets_of_bmesh_elements greps kit.py for the set-comprehension pattern; build-twice test covers the output.

### B203 [A003] - remove_doubles keeps an arbitrary one of two coincident opposite faces; invisible internal faces are exported

| | |
|---|---|
| Severity / area | medium / blender/kit |
| Where | `blender/starship/kit.py` lines export(): bmesh.ops.remove_doubles call (now canonical_order(weld=True)) |
| Status | **fixed** |

*Evidence.* medbed_surgical_table and nozzle_rcs_thruster_cluster still differed between builds after the order fix: two touching boxes (md_sheet / brushed_alu slabs at z=0.3) leave two coincident, oppositely wound faces; remove_doubles dropped one of them, chosen by pointer order (material 3 in one run, 4 in the next). Float noise of 1e-8 in bevel/bisect vertices also differed per run.

*Impact.* Non-reproducible output, plus hidden internal faces that cost triangles and can z-fight.

*Resolution.* Whole catalogue byte-identical across two builds (see A001); total triangles 1,104,397 -> 1,103,960 (internal faces removed).

The same filter also swallowed 'unable to detect undefined names' only by accident.

*Impact.* Real mistakes in 70% of the Python code base (the generators) can never fail CI.

*Resolution.* tests/test_regress_assets.py::UnusedImports (ast based, stdlib) and ::DocsAndCiAgree::test_ci_lint_covers_components.

### B216 [Z001] - Coplanar faces of different materials flicker in 1 model(s) of family `beacon_ceiling`

| Where | `blender/starship/components (family `beacon_ceiling`)` lines family function |
